title: Latency breathing-space scratchbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchbook for a new microburst metric: 'breathing-space' = time for p95 latency to return to baseline after a surge. Trying to capture recovery dynamics that p99 alone misses.

Background / hypothesis:
- Observed that some bursts create a long tail of moderately elevated latency (p95) even after throughput normalizes.
- Hypothesis: this is due to warm-cache starvation + allocator churn + small-coalescing delays (coalescer backoff).
- Goal: measure and compare breathing-space across configurations and create a lightweight probe for CI.

Experiment plan (rough):
1) Workload synth: Poisson base (10 qps) + short spike (200ms window at +150 qps) repeated every 120s, 10 repeats. Payload: seq_len distribution: 70% short (40 tok), 30% long (800 tok). Model: open-gpt-v2-7B (quantized INT8), two serving variants: fastpath (batch=4, kvcache enabled) and slowpath (batch=16, no kvcache priming).
2) Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99, 95th decay time (time for p95 to return within 5% of pre-spike p95), mean CPU/GPU occupancy, queue length, batch size distribution.
3) Probing: inject a single cold-prefill trace every other spike to test cache re-warm impact.

Config matrix (short-hand):
- A: kvcache ON, batch_max=4, prefill_enabled=true, worker_count=8
- B: kvcache OFF, batch_max=4, prefill_enabled=false, worker_count=8
- C: kvcache ON, batch_max=16, prefill_enabled=false, worker_count=4
- D: kvcache ON, batch_max=4, prefill_enabled=true, worker_count=4 (lower capacity)

Preliminary runs (2026-02-15) notes:
- Single node (A100) ephemeral pool, model warm (no model swap).
- Run id: breath-20260215-1
- Short summary: config A shows fastest spike-handling and shortest breathing-space. B shows prolonged elevated p95 (~45s). C shows higher p50/p90 under spike (batch accumulation) but shorter breathing-space than B. D demonstrates interesting behavior: breathing-space ~60s despite lower tail p99.

Sample extracted numbers (aggregated across 10 spikes) - approximate:
- Pre-spike p95 baseline: A=45ms, B=42ms, C=50ms, D=48ms
- Spike peak p99 (during window): A=420ms, B=520ms, C=380ms, D=610ms
- Breathing-space (time to p95 back to baseline+5%): A=12s, B=48s, C=20s, D=62s
- Mean batch size during spike: A=3.6, B=3.9, C=12.1, D=3.4
- KV cache hit-rate (short requests after spike): A=0.78, B=0.18, C=0.74, D=0.81

Quick interpretation:
- KV cache matters a lot for breathing-space — B (no kvcache) has long recovery even when p99 eventually normalizes. Likely due to re-computation of common prefixes causing higher per-token cost that feeds back into queueing.
- Large batch_max (C) reduces peak p99 (amortization) but increases average queueing causing higher p50/p90 during spike; breathing-space shorter than B likely because caching reduces repeated comp work.
- Worker_count reduction (D) reveals that lower parallelism can increase breathing-space significantly even if p99 looks worse; resource saturation + slower drain.

Telemetry artifacts to collect for next runs (TODO):
- Sampled request traces (headers + seq_len + kvcache hit boolean) for first 200 requests after spike.
- Per-batch timing histogram and queue depth timeline with 500ms granularity.
- Per-worker allocation/free counters to detect allocator churn.
- GPU SM utilization traces at 100ms resolution.

Actionable next steps:
- Build small harness that runs 5 cycles of the spike pattern and outputs breathing-space automatically. Integrate as an optional CI probe. (owner: me)
- Add a lightweight per-request kvcache tag in telemetry so we can filter post-spike sequences. (owner: Samir)
- Try hybrid config: kvcache ON + adaptive_batching with burst_threshold=0.4 to force smaller batches during spikes. Hypothesis: reduces p50/p90 spikes without harming amortization. (owner: Maya)
- Re-run on 2-node shard to see cross-node routing impact. If breath grows, routing-induced cold KV distribution might be culprit.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is breathing-space dominated by server-side compute rework or client-side retry behavior? Need end-to-end traces.
- Does quantization interplay (INT8 GEMM) create occasional synchronization stalls visible only in medium tail? Add run with FP16 build.
- How does context length mix affect breathing-space? Current split might be biased; try more fine-grained bins.

Notes to self (scratch):
- When writing CI probe, be conservative: running these for many PRs is expensive. Consider a nightly job instead.
- Slack thread that started this: #runtime-bursts (search for thread id ~Feb 12).
- Related GH: runtime/predictor throttling sketch (PR 4123) — check the admission controller flags.

Rough experiment checklist for repeatable run:
- [ ] provision single A100 node with nvlink disabled (replicate env)
- [ ] deploy model variant open-gpt-v2-7B-int8 (tag v2026-01-20)
- [ ] set traffic generator seed=20260215
- [ ] record prometheus scrape interval to 5s (for graphing)
- [ ] run 10 spikes, collect traces, export to s3://redwood-inference-tests/breathing-space/{run-id} (manual for now)

End notes:
This is intentionally messy — want to capture current intuition and measurement plan. Next pass: formalize metric definition, add small script to ingest Prom metrics and compute breathing-space and CI failure thresholds.

-- Iris
